newsitem.title: UK: Scot walks free after mercy killing of brother.
newsitem.headline: Scot walks free after mercy killing of brother.

text.p: A man walked free from a Scottish court on Monday after admitting to the mercy killing of his dying brother.
The Voluntary Euthanasia Society welcomed the judge's decision but churches expressed alarm after Paul Brady left the court in the arms of sobbing relatives.
Brady, 37, killed his 40-year-old brother James who was suffering from Huntington's Disease, a hereditary illness characterised by dementia.
He gave him extra medication and alcohol before putting a pillow on his face.
The judge, Lord McFadyen, said no jail term was necessary "in the exceptional circumstances", which included a "heartfelt" request for his life to be ended.
Both the Church of Scotland and the Roman Catholic Church voiced alarm over the judgment.
